questions.question: What is the best way to reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn off your phone before you start driving.
Only use your phone to accept incoming calls.
Use your phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your phone before you start driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn off your phone before you start driving and keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: Which statement about distracted driving is true?

options.text: Distracted driving only happens when you are physically distracted, not mentally distracted.
Pre-programming radio stations while driving can increase distraction.
Eating while driving helps you avoid distraction.
You can reduce distraction by avoiding complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can reduce distraction by avoiding complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid complex or emotionally intense conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Remember that mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: What is true about freeway off-ramps for trucks?

options.text: They are usually safe for trucks.
They can be dangerous for trucks.
Trucks should not use them.
Trucks should only use them when following another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be dangerous for trucks.
questions.explanation: Off-ramps have slopes and curves that can be dangerous for trucks. The posted speed limits may be safe for cars but too fast for large or heavily loaded trucks.

questions.question: Which sign shows that a driver is drowsy?

options.text: Your eyes go out of focus on their own.
You have trouble holding your head up.
You drift from lane to lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsy driving include your eyes closing or losing focus, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: What do move over laws require drivers to do?

options.text: Trucks must use the left lane.
All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.
All vehicles must use the left lane.
All vehicles must move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, drivers must leave the lane next to it if possible. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what should you inspect?

options.text: Check that the fluid level is correct.
Make sure the hoses are connected to the battery.
Confirm that the hoses are empty of fluid.
Allow only small leaks to be present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the fluid level is correct.
questions.explanation: Inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level of the power steering system. Check for leaks and repair them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: How should baggage and freight be stored on a bus?

options.text: In a way that lets passengers see the items easily.
In a way that protects riders if items fall or shift.
In the aisle where it will not shift.
In a way that covers the windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that protects riders if items fall or shift.
questions.explanation: Baggage and freight must be stored so the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any window or door in an emergency, and items cannot fall or shift and injure riders.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allows the rear wheels to lock up.
Allows all wheels to lock up.
Helps prevent wheels from locking up.
Alerts other drivers when you are braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps prevent wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: What should you do before checking the engine compartment?

options.text: Release the parking brake.
Block the wheels with chocks.
Start the engine.
Put the gear shift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels with chocks.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, engage the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine compartment before you get in the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do with your turn signals?

options.text: Hide your driving intentions from others.
Only use them if there are vehicles nearby.
Do not use them in construction zones.
Always use them to warn others about your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use them to warn others about your intentions.
questions.explanation: Always communicate your driving intentions to other drivers. Signal before you turn or change lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can a driver slow down?

options.text: Shift into a higher gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Find a hill.
Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear. This will help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Always keep both hands on the steering wheel when turning quickly to avoid a crash. A firm grip on the wheel helps you turn quickly and safely.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the road shoulder is likely to:

options.text: Pay attention to traffic on the road.
Focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
Be exempt from traffic laws.
Not need assistance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Focus on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on their repair and may not notice traffic or other hazards on the road.

questions.question: If a driver feels tired while driving, what should they do?

options.text: Continue driving.
Drink coffee.
Stop and rest.
Drive faster to finish the trip quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, safely leave the road and get some sleep. Coffee and other stimulants are dangerous. They can cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: After starting the engine, how long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal?

options.text: Within a few seconds.
After about a minute.
After about four minutes.
Within 10 minutes of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Watch your gauges after you start the engine. Oil pressure should rise to normal within a few seconds.

questions.question: During a bus ride, what is required about the aisle?

options.text: Carry-on bags may be kept in the aisle.
Passengers may sit in the aisle.
The aisle must be kept clear of obstacles.
Small items can be placed in the aisle if easy to step over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The aisle must be kept clear of obstacles.
questions.explanation: Do not put carry-on bags in doorways or aisles. Nothing should be in the aisle that might cause riders to trip. Secure baggage safely.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distraction that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in a vehicle.
Children on the side of the road.
Construction workers on the side of the road.
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to others may not pay attention to the road. Children may run into the road without looking. Be careful near construction workers. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a traffic concern.

questions.question: If you feel tired and are yawning frequently, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving.
Get some coffee.
Drive faster.
Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Caffeine and other stimulants are not safe. They will wear off and leave you even more tired.

questions.question: To avoid being an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Tailgate other vehicles.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid being aggressive, plan trips realistically and allow extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate or drive slowly in the left lane. Do not gesture at other drivers.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Rely only on traffic control signals.
Never try to outdrive an approaching train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to outdrive an approaching train.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming. Do not assume signals will always warn you. Never try to outdrive a train at a crossing.
